memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then make fifty gold clasps and use them to fasten the curtains together so that the tabernacle is a unit." - Exodus 26:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Fifty golden clasps held the curtains together so that the tabernacle would be "a unit" — one whole, not a collection of pieces. The clasps were small compared to the vast curtains, yet without them the covering would fall apart. Something had to hold it all together.

There is a picture here worth pausing on. What makes God's people one is not our similarity, our preferences, or our personalities. Left to ourselves, we drift apart easily. Something outside of us must do the holding. Paul writes that in Christ "all things hold together" (Col 1:17), and it is Christ Himself who unites His church across every difference of background, temperament, and culture.

This is freeing. We do not have to manufacture unity by making everyone the same. The curtains stayed distinct; the clasps did the joining. In the same way, our differences need not be erased for us to be one — we are held together by our shared belonging to Jesus. When relationships in the church feel strained, the answer is not uniformity but a firmer grip on the One who holds us. Keep your eyes on Christ, and you will find yourself closer to His people too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I trying to manufacture unity, or resting in the One who holds us together?
How does shared belonging to Christ change how I view believers who differ from me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the one who holds Your people together. Help me hold fast to You, and to love believers who differ from me because we belong to the same Saviour. Amen.
